title: Capacity Smoothing TCO Simulator
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a working simulator for evaluating Private deployment TCO (on-prem vs. VPC) using a capacity-smoothing heuristic: amortize peaks across a baseline pool + burst layer to reduce committed-reserve cost and map that to license/support bundle choices.

How to use (quick):
- Fill the Demand Profile (monthly active tokens/hour or qps) in the left table.
- Define hardware SKU choices (type, GPU count, effective throughput, hourly cost).
- Set finance params: discount rate, lease vs buy terms, depreciation years, support uplift.
- Toggle smoothing knobs: baseline utilization target (e.g., 60%), burst headroom cap (%), burst price multiplier.
- Choose license/support bundle: Std, Premium, Enterprise; each maps to percent of committed capacity allowed for reserved pricing and to included support hours.

Assumptions (editable):
- Discount rate (real) = 8% 
- On-prem CapEx amortization window = 36 months (default), option to shift to 60 months for hardware finance.
- VPC equivalent hourly GPU cost = $3.50/GPU-hour (baseline mfr-quoted spot/credit excluded).
- On-prem total cost = HW + Data-center (power + rack) + ops headcount allocation + sw license fee + support.
- License tiers:
  * Std: Per-GPU runtime license $400/month, 8x5 support (SLAs: email), no on-call.
  * Premium: $850/month, 24x7 incident support, 4 onsite days/year included.
  * Enterprise: $1,600/month, dedicated TAM, 10 onsite days/year.

Input tables (example rows):
- Demand profile (monthly):
  Month	Tokens/hr (avg)	Peak qps	Notes
  2026-01	120M	1,200	post-launch beta
  2026-02	95M	900	seasonal dip
  2026-03	210M	2,100	marketing campaign
  2026-04	130M	1,300	steady-state
  2026-05	150M	1,400	

- Hardware SKUs:
  SKU	GPU	Throughput tokens/hr per GPU	Hourly cost (incl infra ops)
  A100-80GB	8x	25M	$8.50
  H100-94GB	8x	38M	$12.00
  L4-48GB	8x	10M	$3.00

Smoothing logic (implemented as formulas in the sheet):
1) Compute required raw GPUs per month = ceil(peak_tokens/hr / throughput_per_gpu).
2) Baseline commit = max( ceil(avg_tokens/hr / throughput_per_gpu), ceil(baseline_util_target * required_raw_gpus) )
3) Burst capacity needed = max(0, required_raw_gpus - baseline_commit)
4) Map baseline_commit to reserved price (on-prem = amortized HW + fixed ops; VPC reserved = 0.7 * on-demand hourly; burst uses on-demand or spot price multiplier)
5) License allocation rules: Std applies to baseline only up to baseline_commit; bursts billed at overage license rate (license_pro_rata_multiplier) or qualifying for temporary burst licenses if Enterprise selected.

Finance outputs (cells):
- Monthly cost breakdown: HW amortization, power/cooling, network egress, ops FTE alloc (FTE $/month), license, support, burst premium, total monthly TCO, per-token unit cost.
- Payback/IRR: If customer pays an initial setup + license commit, compute months to payback vs VPC baseline and 3-yr IRR.

Sample scenario (quick read):
- Baseline target 60% util, burst cap 1.5x baseline (i.e., can burst to 150% of baseline).
- Using H100 SKU and demand profile above, simulator shows:
  * Baseline GPUs needed: 6 (amortized hardware monthly = $28k/month incl ops)
  * Burst average (over campaign months): 3 GPUs on-demand at $12/hr -> burst premium = $8.6k/month
  * License cost (Premium) = $850 * 6 = $5.1k/month + overage license = $900/month
  * Total monthly TCO (on-prem financed 36mo) = $42.6k -> $0.00035 per token
  * VPC equivalent (same capacity cold-start, no amortization) = $47.2k/month -> 11% higher for this profile
  * If amortization stretched to 60mo, on-prem reduces to $36.9k/month -> 22% savings vs VPC.

Sensitivity modules (tabs):
- Utilization swing: recompute TCO when baseline util in [40%, 80%] (step 5%).
- Burst price multiplier: factor 1.0..3.0 (on-demand vs premium spot).
- License delta: Std vs Premium vs Enterprise, toggle included burst allowances (Enterprise allows 20% burst without overage).
- Ops staffing: show break-even FTE allocation where on-prem makes sense given headcount cost.

Optimization recommendations (draft notes):
- For customers with >65% steady utilization, recommend longer amortization window + larger baseline commit to capture capex leverage.
- For highly spiky workloads (campaigns), recommend: smaller baseline + VPC burst or Enterprise license with burst credits bundled (saves per-token license overage).
- Bundle-savvy pricing: introduce a "burst-credit" add-on SKU priced at $X/month that covers up to Y hours of burst at reduced license overage; simplifies decision boundary versus raw VPC.
- Offer an "Ops-light" managed option: Redwood manages hardware pool (on-prem rack or hosted colocation) with fixed ops fee; reduces customer ops FTE allocation and shifts economics in favor of on-prem for mid-size deals.

Open questions / To-Do (working backlog):
- Validate GPU throughput assumptions with serving-runtime bench (PR #4523 referenced above).
- Add network egress models by region (APAC vs NA) to get more accurate VPC comparisons.
- Add tax and CAPEX financing variants: lease vs loan vs outright purchase (impacting WACCs and monthly amortization).
- Explore licensing structures that allow ephemeral license keys for burst pool to reduce overage costs.
- Run automated sweep across 200 synthetic demand traces to produce contour heatmap (savings vs VPC) — needs compute from infra team.

Notes on provenance and limitations:
- This is a working experiment: numbers are placeholders and rely on bench-derived throughput. Use only for internal pre-sales modelling until validated with SRE bench tests.
- Sheet contains helper columns with formulas referencing 'throughput_profile' tab — do not delete.
